Storage

A strongroom off the pack for gear you mean to keep for later: it takes no pack space, auto-salvage never touches it, and the vault may choose from it. Send a piece here from its window; take it back the same way. Emptied when you ascend.

Rune pouch

Runewords need three runes. Inscribe them from an item's window. One per item, permanent.

Collection

Unique weapons and set armour you've found. Area uniques drop from that area's monsters, boss uniques from bosses (best odds on the first kill), set pieces in their home area once its boss is down, and hold relics from chests.

Bestiary

Every kill counted by kind. A thousand of a kind teaches you where it is soft; ten thousand how it moves; a hundred thousand more than there are. Each lesson is a permanent edge against that kind.

Prayers drain points while active. Points refill slowly only when no prayer is lit. Each bone restores 8. Points cap at 30 + combat level.

The Coach

What the champion does on their own, here and while you are away. Every switch is earned.

Combat style

Your weapon decides this. Swords and axes fight in Melee on Attack and Strength; bows, crossbows and knives fight in Ranged; wands, staves, orbs and tomes fight in Magic. Each trains its own skill and needs its own level to wield.

Training weapons

Claim a free Bronze weapon to fight in any style. Training weapons can be wielded and upgraded like any other, but are worth nothing to sell or salvage.

Stance

Accurate trains Attack, Aggressive trains Strength, Defensive trains Defence, Controlled splits it. In Ranged or Magic those feed that skill instead. Hitpoints always trains.

Feats

Deeds pay once. Some carry a title: wear it on your name plate.

Goals for this realm alone; the board wipes clean when you ascend. Shards and jewels for the taking.

Disciplines

How to playthe short version

The idea — Combat runs on its own. You coach: stance, gear, when to eat, where to fight, and when to pull the boss. Damage you deal trains your skills. Monsters drop gold, food, gear and chests.

Getting further — Kill enough in an area to unlock its boss; beat the boss to open the next area. Weapons need Attack, armour needs Defence. Salvage junk for scrap and raise favourite pieces at the Forge.

The fight screen — The two pools at the top of the scene are your health and the monster's. The orbs along the foot are your prayers (tap to light or snuff the set you last chose; tap the number to pick prayers), food, special attack (it glows when it has the energy; tap to loose it), potions and the boss. The map icon opens the realm; the speech bubble shows or hides the chronicle.

Dots — A gold dot on a menu or a room chip means something waits there. The strip above the realm map lists what is worth doing right now.

Keys — 1–5 menus · Space special · E eat · B bury bones.

Away — The hold fights on without you for up to eight hours, at the area you left it in. Come back to a summary of what fell, and a chronicle line when the phone only put the page to sleep.

The opening — A gold line above the scene walks a new champion through the first ten minutes, one hint at a time, each with a button that goes where it points. The ✕ hides them.

What's newthe last few builds, and where each thing lives
The menuswhere everything lives

Worn — Your champion: the Equipment window with the paperdoll and stat sheet, and the pack beneath it with filters, chests, salvage and sell-junk, and the auto-salvage rules.

Vault — The Medallion; Storage with the Mimic, the Vault building and the rune pouch beneath the strongroom; the Collection with the Bestiary under it.

Train — Skills with Prayer beside them and the combat style, training weapons and stance; Feats with the bounty board, the Road, realm deeds, Disciplines and Mastery; Ascension with the trials, the altar, the Heirloom and the Hall of Ancestors.

March — The realm map, pinned with everything there is to do, and the area list beneath it.

Hold — Buildings with the Dynasty at the top; the Barracks with the siege above the roster and the companion armoury; the Peddler with his licence.

Fighting wellprayer, food, potions, defence

The Coach — Under Train › Skills: switches for what the champion does alone. Loose the special when charged, challenge the boss each time the count is met, march on to the next area when your hit chance there clears your mark, relight prayers, retreat when the food is gone, and double time. Each is earned: combat 20 for the special, the first boss for the boss, the first ascension for marching, combat 30 for prayers, three deaths for retreat, every area cleared for double time. All of them run while you are away too. A death drops you back one area; the away window says who killed you and how often they hit.

The Night Watch — The scene follows your clock: dusk from seven, dark from nine, dawn at five. By night a wraith, a moth-witch and a grave hound walk every area, stronger than its day monsters, dropping bones and sometimes a chest. A hundred of a kind by night teaches you their ways: more drops after dark from every one of them. The Bestiary keeps a page for them, and a night away is a night's hunting.

Goblins — Now and then one scurries onto the field with something it should not have: a sack of coin, a bag of gear, a satchel of runes, a strongbox, or a pouch of jewels once you hold the medallion. It cannot be killed and never swings back. For sixty seconds every blow, yours or a companion's, shakes loose a share of what it carries; hard blows and specials shake more. Then it bolts, dropping one last thing on the way out.

Prayer — Light prayers for accuracy, damage, defence, regen or protection, from the prayer orb under the fight or the Prayer section under Train. They drain points; bones from kills restore them, and auto-bury is on by default. Smite, Stone Skin and Sight join from combat 55.

Food and potions — Eat from the orb or automatically below the threshold set under Prayer. Draughts are brewed at the Larder and drunk from the potion orb.

Damage reduction — From gear, prayers, draughts, creeds, the medallion and a defender companion, capped at 70%; a landed blow always costs at least a point, and reduction below nothing raises the damage taken.

Matched kits — Helm, body, legs, gloves and boots all of one tier pay +4% to every combat roll.

Elites — One monster in twenty comes up Swift, Stony, Venomous, Gilded or Hulking, with twice the drops.

Difficulty — Hard, Expert and Master open as you clear areas and pay more gold, drops and XP for tougher monsters. Nightmare opens at Dynasty rank 1 and Torment at realm 15; Torment alone drops seals from ordinary monsters and can leave a worn jewel Flawless.

Gearforge, runes, uniques, tiers

The Forge — Reroll a piece's affixes for gold and scrap, or temper it up a rarity: Fine, Superior, Masterwork, Legendary, then Mythic with five affixes. Mythic also costs three Starsteel ingots. Uniques and set pieces keep what they were made with. A Mythic at the forge cap climbs one rung a realm for shards, to +25.

Starsteel — An area boss gives up a bar the first time it falls, and sometimes after, more often on the harder tiers. Tower wardens carry it too, and the peddler sells it under a licence.

The Long Hunt — Ten thousand kills in an area wake its trophy: a named monster far above the area's level, waiting on the March map (tap the area). Each of the eight drops one piece of the Pyrelord set, a set that exists nowhere else, eight pieces and no shield; after the eight come the three weapons. Every ten thousand more kills the trophy returns. Kills count for life, across ascensions. The full set with a Pyrelord weapon is a form of its own.

Runes — Drop from monsters, bosses and the tower; three make a Runeword you inscribe onto a piece for a permanent bonus. Tempest, Warden, Hunter and Pilgrim join in the mid game. Every slot has a fighting word: Ironhide, Grip, Titan and Stride for legs, gloves and boots, Crown for the head, Mantle for the cape, Talisman and Bloodoath for the jewellery, and Sovereign (Blood, Star, Star) for any piece.

Uniques and sets — 30 named weapons with their own bonuses and 10 four-piece armour sets with 2- and 4-piece bonuses. Gold-bordered in the pack, never auto-salvaged. Area uniques drop from that area's monsters, boss uniques from bosses, set pieces in their home area once its boss is down.

Storage — A strongroom beside the pack: gear sent there takes no pack space, is never auto-salvaged, and the Vault may pick from it. Ascension empties it.

Obsidian and Starsteel tiers — Two tiers past Dragon, at Defence 75 and 90 (Basilisk and Phoenix hide for rangers, Voidweave and Celestial robes for mages). Drops reach Obsidian from realm 3 and Starsteel from realm 8; the tower at floors 64 and 72, the Abyss at waves 32 and 36.

The Sovereign harness — One set for a champion with 99 in every combat skill, nine pieces and a weapon for each style. It drops only once you have them: from any boss at about one in three hundred, the Elder Wyrm at one in sixty, tower wardens past floor 100 at one in forty.

The Forge of Souls — Inside the Forge card. A duplicate unique or set piece renders to essence from its item window; ten essence and gold forge any unique you have found, at Mythic.

Companionsthe roster and the barracks

Songs — The Mariachis learn songs by hearing them: a corrido from a goblin bolting with its bag, a dirge over a slain nemesis, a reel in the Elder Wyrm's death rattle. Pick the one they play in the Barracks. A song changes the fight's rhythm, not its numbers: every third swing a special, lifesteal into a ward, goblins lingering ninety seconds. They play only while the band is in the field.

Earning them — The hold's three are free. Six come from the feats board (Tiger, Fairy, Assassin, Knight, Ent, Excalibur), five drop from bosses (the Necromancer from the Sewer Wyrm, the Barbarian from Warlord Gunnar, the Bear from the Frost Matriarch, the Imp from the Ashborn Overlord, the Golden Dragon from the Elder Wyrm). The Mariachis are bought from the peddler once you have bought anything else from him: three men, one companion, both places in the field.

The field — Two fight beside you, the second slot at Barracks level 2. The rest hold the barracks, run errands and expeditions, and all of them defend a siege.

The Barracks room — One row per companion; tap one for its kit, talents and errands in one window, with Train, Swear, Field and Dismiss at the bottom. The companion armoury button sells and fits seven-piece kits: power and attack sharpen blows, defence shields you, strength is flat damage, prayer widens your pool.

Talents — At levels 5, 10 and 15 a companion picks one of two talents for its role; every option's description shows before the choice.

Oaths and expeditions — At level ten and twenty million gold a companion swears an oath: power ×1.3, never dismissed. Twelve- and twenty-four-hour expeditions bring back a jewel, a cursed scroll and Starsteel.

The Holdbuildings, siege, peddler

Buildings — Raise the Forge, Salvage Yard, Larder, War Chest and Barracks with gold and scrap for permanent perks. Every card folds to its header; tap to open it.

Cooking — The Larder turns raw food into meals: three shrimp into a stew, two trout into a pie that restores prayer, a lobster, swordfish and shark into a feast that charges the special.

The Vault — A sixth building in Storage, priced for the Mimic's purse, that keeps one, two, then three chosen items through an ascension.

Dynasty — Raise all five buildings to their top and the hold can be razed; it must be built again, and comes back a rank stronger for good.

Sieges — Once a real day the horde comes to the gates for ten minutes, from the card above the roster. Kill fast and the walls stand; let one live fifteen seconds and they take a blow. Companions fight twice as often. Hold and the hold pays; fall and a building is wrecked a level.

The Peddler — His cart stands in the Hold, always open, with goods priced for the ground you have reached, each sold once and laid out fresh every hour. Raise his licence and each level adds a line to the cart and takes 8% off every price.

The Marchmap, tower, abyss, road

The Realm — A map of everything there is to do, each thing pinned where it lives and dotted when it waits. Tap a place to go there or to do the thing; the area list sits beneath it.

Tower of Trials — Endless floors. Records every five floors pay a chest; dying just sends you home. Past floor 100 the tower takes realm scaling, pays realm gold, and its wardens carry jewels. Past 200 every floor carries an omen and every tenth warden is a slain nemesis returned.

The Abyss — Beside the tower. Waves, not floors; each raises the run's loot. Bank and leave at any wave, or die and lose it all.

The road — Every quarter hour or so something crosses it with a choice of two, under the battle; ignore it for a minute and you walk on.

Delves — Elites sometimes drop a black-iron key; from the map it opens a door under the current ground, three rooms of two doors each, ending in a chest and better.

Lairs and area mastery — Every area hides a lair; 150 kills of its first monster in a realm open it, and its keeper drops a unique of the area, once a realm. Kills per area across every realm pay back there: gold at 500, drops at 2,000, max hit at 5,000.

Marks and the nemesis — Three named monsters are posted each realm, hunted anywhere; a mark that outlives the realm gains a rank. Once the medallion is forged, a named hunter stalks each realm after three areas are cleared; slay it for gold, shards, Starsteel and a jewel, or let it grow. A nemesis of the third rank sends a lieutenant per area carrying a piece of your last champion's gear.

The Wyrm's phases — From realm 20 the Elder Wyrm fights armoured (a tenth damage until a special cracks it), then burning, then enraged below a quarter; slain past the armour it gives ten shards more.

Feats and trainingboards, disciplines, mastery

Feats and titles — Deeds pay once; some carry a title with a small edge that fits it. Wear it on your name plate.

Bounties — Three posted daily under Feats; claim rewards there, reroll ones you dislike. A contract is posted each Monday beside them: one long goal for the week, paying a unique of a cleared area.

The Road and realm deeds — The Road is a milestone track paid once each, up to the Elder Wyrm. Realm deeds are a second board that wipes every realm: the whole map, three Master clears, the nemesis early, five thousand kills, floor 150, no deaths, a six-hour realm.

Disciplines — At combat level 30, 50 and 70, one of three for your style of fighting; they hold until you ascend, then are chosen again.

Mastery — Passive titles that arrive at set skill levels and feed your real bonuses. Weapon proficiency counts kills with each weapon across realms; 500, 2,000 and 5,000 each teach that weapon's own edge, for good.

Bestiary — Under the Collection. Kills counted by kind; a thousand, ten thousand and a hundred thousand of a kind each teach a permanent edge against it.

Ascensioncreeds, medallion, trials

Vendetta — When the nemesis kills you it takes one piece of what you were wearing and wears it: it shows in their name, and they hit harder for it. Kill them and everything comes back Reclaimed, +4% max hit and +4% XP that only that piece carries. A nemesis that beats you three times flees to the Tower of Trials with all of it and waits on a boss floor past twenty.

The Pretender — Each realm a rival sets out for the throne the day you do, built from the ancestor you beat most recently. They cross the realm in the background; their pin moves on the March map. Slay the Elder Wyrm first and they kneel into the hall with a perk. Let them slay it first and they hold the throne: the altar will not answer until you duel them, on their terms, their perk doubled.

Ascending — At the altar under Train, once the Elder Wyrm is slain. Skills, gear, gold, food and areas reset for permanent shards and a harder, richer realm. Swear one of three creeds offered from forty-three; none is ever lost, every creed sworn stays in force and they stack.

Vows and omens — Before ascending, swear as many vows as you dare for the realm ahead; each is a big gift and a real cost, and each pays 15% more shards. From realm 10 each ascension rolls an omen for the whole realm; shards can buy the next one instead.

The Medallion — Forged on your first ascension, under Vault. Six sockets for six jewel colours; the Elder Wyrm gives one up each realm and deep tower wardens carry them. Fuse duplicates to raise a grade; carve recipes of three runes; two inscriptions carved at once can resonate; a grade-ten stone can be re-cut for a Flawless one, or crack. A nemesis of the fifth rank opens a seventh socket.

Trials — Offered once, right after each ascension: bare hands, alone, iron rules, the silent realm. Begin one and the whole realm is fought under its rules; slay the Elder Wyrm and the time is kept. Refuse and the trials close until you ascend again. Forfeit any time from the card, with nothing lost.

The Heirloom — Forged from a Mythic weapon and two loose jewels; it survives every ascension and inherits one affix from each champion's last weapon, six at most.

Hall of Ancestors — Every ascension leaves a portrait beneath the altar, with a small permanent perk from the skill that champion carried furthest. Any portrait can be challenged to a duel once a realm; beat the ancestor and their perk counts twice until you ascend.

The Mimic — In Storage, under Vault. From realm 10 it eats gold for permanent gifts: the forge cap, max hit and accuracy, hitpoints, attack speed, luck. Each feeding costs more than twice the last, and ascending empties the purse, so feed it before you climb.

Soundeffects, music, volume

Effects — Every cue is made on the spot: a blow landing, a miss, a hit taken, a kill, a chest, a level, prayers lit, the Sovereign's burst. Nothing to download. The first tap on the page wakes the sound.

Volume 60%

Music — Music is a file, not code: the toggle plays music/theme.mp3 beside the game when that file exists, and says so when it does not.

Saveexport, import, reset

Saves every 10 seconds when browser storage is available. Copy the code to move your save elsewhere.
